title: The winds that scatter
hook: by the winds that scatter, and the clouds that carry (51:1–2)

segments.voice: Yesterday's word was juz', one of the Qur'an's thirty parts, and Block C closed. Your line: the middle holds the whole.

Block D: towards the thirtieth part. Over the next ten weeks or so, the path walks from Surah Adh-Dhariyat, the fifty-first, toward the short surahs that close the book. The surahs get shorter and the sound changes: quicker lines, oaths piling up one after another. And the very first thing this block does is swear by something you can't see, only feel on your face: the wind, the thing that scatters.

Surah Adh-Dhariyat opens with four oaths, each a short line in Arabic. Pickthall's translation of the first two: "By those that winnow with a winnowing, And those that bear the burden (of the rain)." Winnowing is an old farm picture: tossing grain in the air so the wind blows the chaff away. Adh-dhariyat are the scatterers, the winds that lift dust and seed and carry them off. Then al-hamilat, the carriers, bearing a heavy load: the clouds, full of rain. Then al-jariyat, those that run easily, and al-muqassimat, those that distribute by command. The verse doesn't say who these are; it gives only what they do. So people asked. A report preserved by the commentators says 'Ali ibn Abi Talib, preaching in Kufa, invited questions, and someone asked about these opening words. He answered: the scatterers are the winds, the carriers are the clouds, the runners are the ships, and the distributors are the angels. Notice the movement. Wind lifts water to the sky. Cloud carries it. Ships run on the water the wind pushes. And angels distribute, by command, the provision all of it brings. Read that way, ordinary weather becomes a chain of delivery. Why open with an oath? In the Qur'an an oath draws attention: look at this, then hear what follows. The next verses answer: what you are promised is true, and the judgment will come. The surah swears by ordinary things in motion to make a claim about something no one can yet see.
screen: `FOUR OATHS, FOUR MOVING THINGS.` · `WINNOWING: WIND THAT LIFTS AND SCATTERS.` · `'ALI: WINDS, CLOUDS, SHIPS, ANGELS.` · `WEATHER AS A CHAIN OF DELIVERY.`

segments.voice: If you can, step outside or open a window; if not, remember the last wind you felt. Notice where it touches, your face, your hands, the back of your neck, and watch for something it moves: a leaf, a curtain, your hair. You only know it by what it moves, and if you pray, you can say subhanallah, glory to Allah, with each gust.
Adh-dhariyat: the winnowing winds of 51:1, which 'Ali read as the first link in a chain of winds, clouds, ships and angels. Today's word.
Your line: by the scattering winds. The unseen is known by what it moves. See you tomorrow.

options: An oath draws attention: look at the wind, then hear what follows.
Because the wind was worshiped in Arabia, and the surah honors it.
Because the surah is mainly a lesson about farming and weather.
